keyMessage.found: CMC controls who holds an account but not how accounts prove who they are, so administrators and vendors can reach HIS, PACS, and Active Directory with a password alone, which is the entry path used against the peer hospital.
keyMessage.closes: Enforce multi-factor authentication (MFA) for all administrator and remote access to Criticality A systems, starting with vendor connections.

categories.whatWorksToday: Administrators use separate admin accounts, staff use single sign-on (SSO) for Microsoft 365, and staff remote access through the virtual private network (VPN) already requires MFA.

strengths.statement: IT runs a working identity management practice that it demonstrated live, which gives a base for a formal joiner, mover, and leaver process.
IT documents identity proofing for new accounts, but the service desk does not verify identity before password or MFA resets.
Administrators use dedicated admin accounts and a written password standard, but the number of administrators is not limited and access is never reviewed.

gapFindings.title: Privileged and vendor access to critical systems relies on passwords alone
gapFindings.statement: CMC controls who holds an account but not how the account proves identity, so the most powerful access paths have the weakest protection.

supportingFacts.fact: Administrators sign in to HIS, PACS, and Active Directory without multi-factor authentication (MFA).
Vendors connect to HIS and PACS through unattended remote desktop sessions.
Microsoft 365 already enforces MFA for administrators and remote access.

extent.notChecked: Microsoft 365 enforces MFA for administrators and remote access only

gapFindings.consequence: A ransomware operator who obtains one administrator or vendor password can encrypt HIS and Active Directory, which tolerate under four hours of downtime with no manual workaround.

likelihood.rationale: MFA is Poor on three Criticality A systems, vendor remote access is open, and a peer hospital suffered ransomware through the same path.

ops.rationale: HIS and Active Directory down beyond tolerance stops patient registration and logon across both hospitals.

fin.rationale: Quick BIA rates HIS financial impact at 4.

legal.rationale: An incident on CII systems with sensitive health data triggers mandatory reporting duties. Timelines follow the Workshop regulatory verification.

rep.rationale: Quick BIA rates HIS reputation impact at 4.

safety.rationale: Loss of HIS delays clinical orders and results for patients in care.

data.rationale: HIS holds more than 100,000 sensitive health records.

notApplicable.find: Covered by GAP-PR.AA-02 for systems outside the sample.

gapFindings.title: MFA is not a required control, and nobody tracks its coverage
gapFindings.statement: No standard makes MFA mandatory and nobody owns its coverage, so systems outside the sample are likely password-only and new systems can go live without MFA.

supportingFacts.fact: The LIS, ERP, and hospital website profiles show no MFA.
IT keeps no record of which systems use MFA.

extent.notChecked: Systems not yet named in the S2 system list

gapFindings.consequence: Each new or unlisted system adds another password-only entry point that nobody tracks, so the exposure grows with every system change.

likelihood.rationale: Inferred with High confidence: the profile shows no MFA on every listed system, but systems outside the list are not confirmed.

ops.rationale: LIS down beyond tolerance delays laboratory results.

fin.rationale: Quick BIA rates ERP financial impact at 4.

rep.rationale: Quick BIA rates LIS and the hospital website at 3.

safety.rationale: Quick BIA rates LIS health and safety impact at 4.

data.rationale: LIS holds sensitive health records at scale.

notApplicable.fix: Fix actions for sampled systems sit in GAP-PR.AA-01. Other systems are fixed after the Find action confirms them.

gapFindings.title: Access is not controlled across the account life cycle
gapFindings.statement: Access rights depend on individuals rather than a governed process, so nobody limits, reviews, or removes access on critical systems in a consistent way.

supportingFacts.fact: No access review ran on HIS, PACS, or Microsoft 365 in the past 12 months.
The number of Active Directory administrators is not limited.
Leaver and reset steps depend on individuals, and the service desk does not verify identity before resets.

extent.notChecked: Full profile not collected for Criticality B and C systems

gapFindings.consequence: Former staff or vendors can keep access to patient data, and a misused account would not be detected through any review.

likelihood.rationale: Harm needs a second event, such as a leaver or a compromised account, and separate admin accounts limit part of the path.

ops.rationale: Misuse of an administrator account on Active Directory can disrupt logon for all systems.

fin.rationale: Fraud or misuse through ERP access stays within the moderate band.

legal.rationale: Unauthorized access to sensitive health data may require notification under the PDPA.

rep.rationale: Local coverage is the likely outcome.

safety.rationale: No direct effect on patient care from this gap alone.

data.rationale: HIS and PACS access exposes more than 100,000 sensitive records.

gapFindings.title: Server room access cannot be evidenced
gapFindings.statement: CMC relies on a client-stated physical access control that leaves no record, so it cannot prove who entered the rooms that hold critical systems.

supportingFacts.fact: IT states that server room access is controlled but provides no access log.
No access review record exists for the server rooms at either hospital.

gapFindings.consequence: After a physical incident, CMC could not identify who had access, which weakens both investigation and accountability.

likelihood.rationale: Evidence gap only: the practice is client-stated and card access exists in part.

ops.rationale: Physical damage to the server room would take HIS and Active Directory down beyond tolerance.

data.rationale: Theft of a server disk would expose sensitive records.

notApplicable.find: The rooms in scope are known.
notApplicable.prevent: IMP-PR.AA-04-01 includes the quarterly review that prevents recurrence.
notApplicable.exceptions: No room is unable to keep access records.

improvementActions.action: Enforce MFA for all administrator accounts and staff remote access on HIS, PACS, Active Directory, and Microsoft 365.
Require MFA and session logging for vendor remote access, and remove unattended remote desktop tools.
List every system with its authentication method and MFA status, starting with Criticality A and B systems.
Approve the Identity and Authentication Standard and add an MFA check to system onboarding and change approval.
Place systems that cannot support MFA behind an MFA gateway or jump host and record a time-bound risk acceptance for each.
Run a first access review on Criticality A systems, privileged accounts first.
Identify privileged, service, and shared accounts on all systems.
Link joiner, mover, and leaver steps to HR records, set a six-month review cycle, and document service desk identity checks before resets.
Store passwords of accounts that cannot be named or removed in a vault with a named owner.
Keep server room access logs and record a quarterly access list review.
